LUK.18.9-10.text: Two men go up to the temple to pray

LUK.18.11-12.text: The Pharisee thanks God that he is not like others

LUK.18.13-14.text: The tax collector asks God for mercy and is accepted

LUK.18.18-21.text: A ruler asks Jesus how to inherit eternal life

LUK.18.22-23.text: Jesus tells the ruler to sell everything and follow him

LUK.18.24-25.text: Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom

LUK.18.26-27.text: Jesus says God can do what people cannot

LUK.18.28-30.text: Jesus promises Peter a reward for following him

LUK.18.31-33.text: Jesus tells the Twelve he will be killed and rise again

LUK.18.34-34.text: The disciples do not understand what Jesus said

LUK.18.35-37.text: A blind beggar learns that Jesus is passing by

LUK.18.38-39.text: The blind man calls to Jesus and will not be silent

LUK.18.40-41.text: The blind man asks Jesus to let him see again

LUK.18.42-43.text: Jesus heals the blind man and the people praise God

LUK.19.1-2.text: Jesus enters Jericho; Zacchaeus is a rich tax collector

LUK.19.3-4.text: Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus

LUK.19.5-7.text: Jesus goes to Zacchaeus’s house and the people grumble

LUK.19.8-10.text: Zacchaeus gives to the poor; Jesus came to save the lost

LUK.19.11-12.text: Jesus tells a parable about a nobleman going far away

LUK.19.13-15.text: The nobleman gives servants money, then returns as king

LUK.19.16-17.text: The first servant earns ten minas and is rewarded

LUK.19.18-19.text: The second servant earns five minas and is rewarded

LUK.19.20-21.text: Another servant hid the mina because he feared the master

LUK.19.22-23.text: The master calls the servant wicked and judges him

LUK.19.24-25.text: The master gives the servant’s mina to the one with ten

LUK.19.26-27.text: The king gives more to those who have and punishes enemies

LUK.19.28-28.text: Jesus goes on ahead up to Jerusalem

LUK.19.29-31.text: Jesus sends two disciples to bring a colt

LUK.19.32-36.text: The disciples bring the colt, and Jesus rides it

LUK.19.37-38.text: The disciples joyfully praise God and call Jesus King

LUK.19.39-40.text: Some Pharisees want Jesus to silence the disciples

LUK.19.41-42.text: Jesus weeps because Jerusalem missed the way to peace

LUK.19.43-44.text: Jesus says enemies will destroy Jerusalem

LUK.19.45-46.text: Jesus drives the sellers out of the temple

LUK.19.47-48.text: Jesus teaches daily, and leaders plan to kill him

LUK.20.1-2.text: Leaders ask Jesus by what authority he acts

LUK.20.3-4.text: Jesus asks the leaders where John’s baptism came from

LUK.20.5-6.text: The leaders discuss how to answer Jesus’ question

LUK.20.7-8.text: The leaders do not answer, so Jesus refuses to answer

LUK.20.9-10.text: Jesus tells of tenants who beat the owner’s servant

LUK.20.11-12.text: The tenants mistreat two more of the owner’s servants

LUK.20.13-14.text: The owner sends his son, but the tenants plan to kill him

LUK.20.15-16.text: The tenants kill the son and lose the vineyard

LUK.20.17-18.text: Jesus says the rejected stone has become the cornerstone

LUK.20.19-20.text: Leaders want to arrest Jesus and send spies

LUK.20.21-22.text: The spies ask Jesus if people should pay taxes to Caesar

LUK.20.23-24.text: Jesus asks whose image is on a denarius

LUK.20.25-26.text: Jesus tells the people to give to Caesar and to God

LUK.20.27-28.text: The Sadducees ask Jesus about a brother’s widow

LUK.20.29-33.text: The Sadducees ask whose wife the widow will be

LUK.20.34-36.text: Jesus says people in the resurrection do not marry

LUK.20.37-38.text: Jesus says God is the God of the living

LUK.20.39-40.text: The scribes praise Jesus and stop asking questions

LUK.21.5-6.text: Jesus says the temple stones will be thrown down

LUK.21.7-9.text: Jesus warns the disciples not to be deceived

LUK.21.10-11.text: Jesus describes wars, earthquakes and signs from heaven

LUK.21.12-13.text: Jesus says believers will be seized and become witnesses

LUK.21.14-15.text: Jesus tells the disciples not to worry about defending themselves

LUK.21.16-19.text: Jesus says the disciples will be hated but must endure

LUK.21.20-22.text: Jesus tells people in Judea to flee from Jerusalem

LUK.21.23-24.text: Jesus warns of great distress and captivity in Jerusalem

LUK.21.25-26.text: Jesus describes signs in the sky and fear on earth

LUK.21.27-28.text: People will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud

LUK.21.29-31.text: Jesus uses the fig tree to teach about the kingdom

LUK.21.32-33.text: Jesus says his words will never pass away

LUK.21.34-35.text: Jesus warns the disciples to be ready for that day

LUK.21.36-36.text: Jesus urges the disciples to keep watch and pray

LUK.21.37-38.text: Jesus teaches at the temple every day

LUK.22.3-4.text: Satan enters Judas, who talks with the chief priests

LUK.22.5-6.text: The chief priests agree to pay Judas to betray Jesus

LUK.22.7-9.text: Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover

LUK.22.10-11.text: Jesus tells Peter and John how to find the house

LUK.22.12-13.text: Peter and John find the upper room and prepare the Passover

LUK.22.14-16.text: Jesus eats the Passover with the apostles

LUK.22.17-18.text: Jesus shares the cup with the apostles

LUK.22.19-20.text: Jesus gives the apostles the bread and the cup

LUK.22.21-23.text: Jesus says one of the apostles will betray him

LUK.22.24-25.text: The disciples argue about who is the greatest

LUK.22.26-27.text: Jesus tells the disciples that the greatest must serve

LUK.22.28-30.text: Jesus promises his disciples a kingdom and thrones

LUK.22.31-32.text: Jesus prays that Peter’s faith will not fail

LUK.22.33-34.text: Jesus says Peter will deny him three times

LUK.22.35-36.text: Jesus tells the disciples to get a purse, bag and sword

LUK.22.37-38.text: Jesus says Scripture about him must come true

LUK.22.39-40.text: Jesus tells the disciples to pray about temptation

LUK.22.41-42.text: Jesus prays that the Father’s will be done

LUK.22.43-44.text: An angel strengthens Jesus as he prays in anguish

LUK.22.45-46.text: Jesus finds the disciples asleep and urges prayer

LUK.22.47-48.text: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss

LUK.22.49-51.text: A disciple cuts off a servant’s ear and Jesus heals it

LUK.22.52-53.text: Jesus speaks to the leaders who came to arrest him

LUK.22.54-55.text: Jesus is taken to the high priest’s house; Peter follows

LUK.22.56-58.text: Peter twice says he does not know Jesus

LUK.22.59-60.text: Peter denies Jesus a third time and the rooster crows

LUK.22.61-62.text: Jesus looks at Peter, and Peter weeps bitterly

LUK.22.66-68.text: The leaders ask Jesus if he is the Christ

LUK.22.69-71.text: The leaders ask if Jesus is the Son of God

LUK.23.1-2.text: The leaders take Jesus to Pilate and accuse him

LUK.23.3-5.text: Pilate finds no basis for a charge against Jesus

LUK.23.8-10.text: Herod questions Jesus, but Jesus gives no answer

LUK.23.11-12.text: Herod mocks Jesus and sends him back to Pilate

LUK.23.13-14.text: Pilate tells the leaders he finds Jesus not guilty

LUK.23.15-17.text: Pilate says Jesus has done nothing deserving death

LUK.23.18-19.text: The crowd shouts for Pilate to release Barabbas

LUK.23.20-22.text: Pilate again tries to release Jesus, but the crowd refuses

LUK.23.23-25.text: Pilate frees Barabbas and hands Jesus to the crowd

LUK.23.26-26.text: Soldiers make Simon of Cyrene carry Jesus’ cross

LUK.23.27-28.text: Jesus tells the women of Jerusalem to weep for themselves

LUK.23.29-31.text: Jesus warns that hard days are coming

LUK.23.32-32.text: Two criminals are led away with Jesus

LUK.23.33-34.text: Jesus is crucified and asks the Father to forgive

LUK.23.35-35.text: The rulers mock Jesus as people watch

LUK.23.36-38.text: Soldiers mock Jesus, and a sign calls him King

LUK.23.39-41.text: One criminal insults Jesus; the other defends him

LUK.23.42-43.text: Jesus promises the criminal a place in Paradise

LUK.23.44-45.text: Darkness covers the land and the temple veil tears

LUK.23.46-47.text: Jesus dies and a Roman officer praises God

LUK.23.48-49.text: People return home sad; Jesus’ friends watch from afar

LUK.23.50-51.text: Joseph, a good Council member, waited for God’s kingdom

LUK.23.52-53.text: Joseph asks for Jesus’ body and buries it in a tomb

LUK.23.54-56.text: Women from Galilee see the tomb and prepare spices

LUK.24.1-3.text: The women find the stone moved and the tomb empty

LUK.24.4-5.text: Two men in shining clothes speak to the women

LUK.24.6-7.text: The men tell the women Jesus has risen

LUK.24.8-10.text: The women tell the Eleven about the empty tomb

LUK.24.11-12.text: The apostles do not believe; Peter runs to the tomb

LUK.24.13-14.text: Two followers of Jesus walk to Emmaus

LUK.24.15-16.text: Jesus joins the two travelers, who do not know him

LUK.24.17-18.text: Cleopas is surprised that Jesus does not know the news

LUK.24.19-20.text: The travelers tell about Jesus of Nazareth and his death

LUK.24.21-21.text: The travelers had hoped Jesus would redeem Israel

LUK.24.22-24.text: The travelers tell about the empty tomb and the angels

LUK.24.25-27.text: Jesus explains from the Scriptures that Christ must suffer

LUK.24.28-29.text: The travelers ask Jesus to stay for the evening

LUK.24.30-32.text: The travelers recognize Jesus as he breaks bread

LUK.24.33-35.text: The two travelers return to Jerusalem and tell the news

LUK.24.36-37.text: Jesus stands among the disciples, who are frightened

LUK.24.38-40.text: Jesus shows the disciples his hands and feet

LUK.24.41-43.text: Jesus eats a piece of fish in front of the disciples

LUK.24.44-44.text: Jesus says the Scriptures about him must come true

LUK.24.45-47.text: Jesus opens the disciples’ minds to understand Scripture

LUK.24.48-49.text: Jesus calls the disciples witnesses and promises power

LUK.24.50-51.text: Jesus blesses the disciples and is taken up to heaven

LUK.24.52-53.text: The disciples worship Jesus and praise God in the temple
